source_snapshot.procedure:

    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Enter BMC Web UI -> Click tab "Dashboard"
And also enter "Server Health" -> "Sensor Reading"

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sensor get 'PWR_MB_CPU0_, PWR_MB_CPU1_' 2>&1; echo ---SDR-FALLBACK---; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sdr elist 2>&1 | head -100
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: returns FULL raw `ipmitool (OOB lanplus) sensor get "<SENSOR>"` reading + threshold; user judges (read-only).

historical_reviews.deepseek: YES passes the comma-separated prefixes as one literal sensor name, so it cannot retrieve or prove either CPU power family. It also assumes one reading per CPU without resolving the suffix members, quantity semantics, socket mapping, telemetry source or workload-dependent acceptance.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly rejects the combined command but treats each trailing-underscore label as one exact sensor. Historical CPU power-monitor cases explicitly match `PWR_MB_CPU0_*` and `PWR_MB_CPU1_*`, showing these are presumptive prefixes for potentially multiple rail or aggregate members. V3.1 therefore requires a Project-authoritative family inventory before claiming coverage.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 896/2291 accepts the combined literal command and output presence without enumerating either prefix family, defining each suffix/quantity/rail, or binding members to sockets and telemetry sources.
historical_reviews.related_source_cases: Wistron-BMC-00082-V003 uses `PWR_MB_CPU0_~PWR_MB_CPU1_` for workload-responsive sensor behavior, while later CPU-management cases grep `PWR_MB_CPU0_*` and `PWR_MB_CPU1_*` plus CPU aggregate names. Those references clarify prefix intent but do not define this platform's complete family or authorize workload here.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No sequence-1058 draft exists in the invalidated 1,000-record run.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 preserves the incomplete labels; ED-34 treats member inventory, rail/quantity/socket mapping, operating condition and Script as readiness; ED-35 keeps this Sensor Page check passive without CPU stress or power-policy changes; ED-38 requires protected complete evidence, no clear/write/retry and engineer-owned verdict. Wistron I2C/I3C ownership keeps VR/PMBus telemetry in BMC/platform scope unless Project SPEC says otherwise.

original_test_intent: Verify every Project-defined motherboard CPU power telemetry record under the `PWR_MB_CPU0_` and `PWR_MB_CPU1_` prefixes is present and correctly displayed in Dashboard and Server Health > Sensor Reading, with each member bound to the intended socket, rail or aggregate quantity, units, status and supported thresholds.
original_method: Obtain the authoritative member list for both prefixes, map every suffix to CPU socket, rail/aggregate boundary and BMC telemetry source, then compare complete passive raw/UI fields with member-specific limits under a recorded CPU population, workload and power-policy state. Preserve logs and do not create load.
manual_activity: The platform/power owner enumerates all suffix members for both CPU prefixes, defines each electrical boundary and maps it to socket and telemetry source. Automation can collect the passive family records and UI rows; a human confirms the workload/power-policy context and owns the verdict. No CPU stress, policy or firmware change is authorized.
required_inputs: Motherboard/CPU/VR PN and revision, BIOS/BMC/CPU microcode and exact two-socket population
Complete `PWR_MB_CPU0_*` and `PWR_MB_CPU1_*` member names with suffix definitions
Per-member CPU socket, VR rail or package/board boundary, quantity type and units
Per-member power-monitor or VR controller, bus/mux/address/page/register, scaling, averaging window and update rate
Stable SDR and UI identities plus tolerance, thresholds/hysteresis, status, stale and absent-socket rules
Recorded CPU workload/processes, C-state/frequency, power profile/caps, VR state and system input power
Validated protected ipmitool/API/browser access and pinned reviewed `sensor.git` revision/checksum or manual method
safety_requirements: Do not clear SEL, kernel, machine-check, VR or power logs; existing evidence is relevant.
Do not pass `'PWR_MB_CPU0_, PWR_MB_CPU1_'` as one sensor name and do not assume the two prefixes are exact records. Enumerate all approved members and query each separately.
Do not equate board input, VR input/output, CPU package power, voltage, current and energy. Record the electrical boundary, quantity and averaging window for each suffix.
Treat PMBus/I2C/I3C and VR monitoring as BMC/platform scope; host package-energy telemetry can corroborate only with approved boundary and time-window equivalence.
Do not start CPU stress, change governor/C-state/power cap, write VR/threshold settings, flash firmware or reboot. Record the existing operating condition.

Do not truncate inventory, expose passwords with `-P`, assume cipher 17 or execute the inaccessible Script. Stop without automatic retry on unknown suffixes, missing/swapped members, stale data or raw/UI/reference disagreement.
agent_execution_scope: Validate the two prefix families, complete member/quantity/socket/controller map, target, client, vendor reference and Script; build a member-level expectation matrix.

Query every approved member independently with full SDR/controller identity, value, units, threshold capability, status, averaging window and timestamp; capture each unchanged Dashboard and Server Health row.
Record CPU population, processes/load, C-state/frequency, power profile/caps, VR state and system input power; compare only matching electrical boundaries and synchronized windows.
Preserve raw/redacted evidence and logs; perform no clear, CPU stress, power-policy/cap/C-state, VR/threshold/firmware change, automatic retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve the complete suffix/member inventory and CPU0/CPU1 socket, rail/boundary and management-source mapping.
Define member-specific quantity, scaling/window, limits/tolerance, thresholds/status/freshness and absent-socket behavior; approve any host telemetry equivalence and tool/Script.
Review every member rather than two assumed values and issue the formal verdict without substituting package power for board/VR rails or one socket for the other.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Unfit: `ipmitool sensor get` accepts one exact record, not a comma-separated pair of prefixes, and the trailing underscores likely denote families. The command omits member inventory and electrical semantics; its fallback is truncated, credential-exposing and cipher-assumptive.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Enumerate exact approved members for both prefixes from complete sensor inventory and Project specification, query each via protected read-only access, and correlate all UI rows with socket, rail/quantity and operating-condition evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Both preserved prefix labels, both WebUI paths, readability/specification Criteria, generic clear text, Script URL, DeepSeek command and 1/0-minute estimates remain unchanged; Review expands them only in the overlay after Project definition.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a member-level matrix grouped by CPU0 and CPU1, keyed by exact suffix, socket, electrical boundary and telemetry controller; compare complete raw/API and UI fields with member-specific rules under a synchronized recorded CPU/power state.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The exact motherboard, two-socket population and BMC/SDR/WebUI power-telemetry implementation documented by the Project.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record motherboard, CPU/microcode, BIOS/BMC/SDR/WebUI, VR/power-monitor firmware, management client and Script revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Motherboard power tree and socket map, VR/power-monitor specification, BMC telemetry/SDR definitions, CPU power-policy recipe and WebUI schema.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Treats the labels as prefixes requiring complete family enumeration instead of two exact records, and adds electrical-boundary and averaging-window evidence while preserving passive display coverage.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Static readings do not validate workload response, CPU performance, power caps, VR protection, energy accounting, threshold events or shutdown behavior.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Complete member inventory, socket/rail/controller map, member-specific acceptance, synchronized passive state, protected tool or reviewed Script and evidence contract.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Power quantities at different boundaries and time windows can legitimately disagree; family membership may vary by board/BMC revision and an absent CPU may remove several records.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use Redfish/OEM, VR vendor or host CPU telemetry as approved alternatives/corroboration only while preserving the original ipmitool method, recording interface/version/quantity/boundary/window and reason, obtaining engineer approval and proving equivalent complete member, identity, value, threshold, status and freshness coverage. Host package power is not automatically equivalent to motherboard or VR telemetry.
expected_evidence: Motherboard/CPU/BIOS/BMC identity and exact CPU0/CPU1 physical socket/package population
Complete approved member list for both prefixes with suffix, socket, rail/package/board boundary, quantity, units and stable SDR/UI mapping
Power-monitor/VR controller bus/mux/address/page/register, scaling, averaging/update window and complete separate raw values, threshold capability, status and timestamps
Redacted Dashboard/Server Health rows plus recorded processes/load, C-state/frequency, power profile/caps, VR state and synchronized system power with boundary-correct comparisons

Explicit missing/extra/unknown-suffix/absent-socket/stale/divergent disposition, pinned Script/tool evidence, no-clear/no-stress-or-policy-change/no-retry proof, final CPU/VR/BMC health and engineer-owned family verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The trailing underscores and comma make the exact member set incomplete, but the Items, UI Procedure and Criteria consistently target CPU0/CPU1 motherboard power families. Project-defined enumeration resolves execution readiness without changing the preserved source or creating a contradictory purpose.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The passive two-socket power-family display purpose is identifiable, and related source evidence supports prefix semantics. Project telemetry documentation can supply members and acceptance, so the review is not permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Changes YES to PACKAGE, rejects the combined literal command and requires all exact prefix members rather than two assumed records.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains hybrid classification but materially corrects the one-record-per-prefix assumption using related wildcard-based CPU power cases.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces command-presence reasoning with member enumeration, electrical-boundary/socket/controller mapping and synchronized UI/spec evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Uses related cases only to identify likely prefix semantics; it does not import their workload stimulus or guessed member set.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No prior invalid draft exists for this sequence.

review_improvement: Prevents an invalid comma query, incomplete family sample or mismatched package/rail quantity from being presented as CPU0/CPU1 power coverage, and prevents CPU stress or policy changes from being added to a passive Sensor Page test.
independent_technical_reasoning: The terminal underscores and later wildcard filters show these labels are best treated as sensor-family prefixes, not necessarily two complete record names. CPU power may be reported at several non-equivalent boundaries and averaging windows, so every suffix must be decoded and compared only to its own specification under synchronized passive state.
